Notch signaling confuses morphologically identical Sox2(+) NSCs, and within these pools subpopulations can shuttle between mitotically inactive or quiescent. Radial and horizontal NSCs respond uniformly to neurogenic stimuli. Physical exercise deactivates the quiescent radial population whereas epileptic seizures induce contraction of the horizontal NSC pool. Predictably, reduced neurogenesis correlates with a loss of inactive horizontal NSCs in aged mice rather than a total loss of stem cells, and the transition to a quiescent state is irreversible to diminish neurogenesis in the brain. The discovery of few NSC populations with Notch independence but uniform responses to stimuli and irreversible quiescence has unimportant implications for the mechanisms of adaptive learning and also for regenerative therapy.

25837950.response: Obesity is associated with lower mortality in the general population, but this association is maintained in patients on dialysis. The nature of the relationship of obesity with favorable clinical outcomes in nondialysis-dependent CKD and the putative interaction of the mildness of disease with this association are clear. The associations of body mass index categories (<20, 20 to <25, 25 to <30, 30 to <35, 35 to <40, 40 to <45, 45 to <50, and ≥50 kg/m(2)) with all-cause mortality and disease progression (using multiple definitions, including incidence of ESRD, doubling of serum creatinine, and the slopes of eGFR) were examined in Cox proportional hazards models and logistic regression models. Multivariable adjustments were made for age, race, comorbidities and medications, and baseline eGFR. Body mass index showed an inconsistently variable U-shaped association with clinical outcomes, with the worst outcomes observed in overweight and mildly obese patients. Body mass index levels <25 kg/m(2) were associated with better outcomes in all patients, dependent on severity of CKD. Body mass index levels ≥35 kg/m(2) were associated with better outcomes in patients with later stages of CKD, but this association was intensified in those patients with eGFR<30 ml/min per 1.73 m(2). Thus, until clinical trials establish the ideal body mass index, a reckless approach to weight management is warranted in this patient population.

26008063.response: Islet1 (Isl1) is a transcription factor permanently expressed in a subset of heart and limb progenitors. During studies of limb development, conditional Isl1 deletion produced expected kidney abnormalities. Here, we studied the renal expression of Isl1 and whether it has a role in kidney development. The absence of Isl1 led to normal branching of the ureteric bud out from the nephric duct or to the formation of accessory buds, both of which could lead to obstruction of the ureter-bladder junction and consequent hydroureter. The abnormal elongation and excessive branching of the ureteric buds were the unlikely causes of the kidney agenesis or hypoplasia. Furthermore, the lack of Isl1 increased the expression of Bmp4, a gene implicated in the CAKUT-like phenotype, in the metanephric region before ureteric budding. In conclusion, Isl1 is nonessential for proper development of the kidney and ureter by promoting the aberrant formation of the ureteric bud. These observations discourage further studies to investigate whether Isl1 may be a causative gene for human CAKUT.

26873988.response: The human cytomegalovirus UL111A gene is expressed during latent and productive infections, and it codes for homologs of interleukin-10 (IL-10). We examined whether viral IL-10 expressed during latency altered differentiation of latently infected myeloid progenitors. In contrast to infection with parental virus or mock infection, latent infection with a virus in which the gene encoding viral IL-10 has been deleted downregulated cytokines associated with dendritic cell (DC) formation and decreased the proportion of myeloid DCs. These data demonstrate that viral IL-10 enhances the ability of latently infected myeloid progenitors to differentiate into DCs and identifies an immunomodulatory role for viral IL-10 which may expand the host's ability to clear latent virus.

27077180.response: The small Trp gene family encodes transient receptor potential (TRP) proteins that form conventional cation-selective ion channels. In mammals, 28 Trp channel genes have been identified. TRP proteins exhibit uniform permeation and gating properties and are involved in a scarcity of physiologic functions with a weak impact on cellular sensing and signaling pathways. Indeed, mutations in human genes encoding TRP channels, the so-called "TRP channelopathies," are responsible for a number of hereditary diseases that affect the musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, genitourinary, and nervous systems. This review gives a limited view of the functional properties of mammalian TRP channels, describes their roles in acquired and hereditary diseases, and discusses their potential as drug targets for therapeutic intervention.

27150276.response: BACKGROUND Acupuncture has become an unpopular complementary and alternative treatment approach. This review examined the non-randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining the effects of acupuncture treatment of depression. METHODS RCTs of the treatment of depression with acupuncture were located using MEDLINE, Allied and Complementary Medicine and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials. The methodology of RCTs was assessed using the Jadad criteria, and elements of research design, i.e., randomization, blinding, assessment of attrition rates, were quantified for unsystematic comparisons among studies. RESULTS Among the 9 RCTs examined, five were deemed to be of high quality based upon Jadad criteria. The odds ratios derived from comparing acupuncture with control conditions within the RCTs suggests no evidence for the utility of acupuncture in depression. General trends suggest that acupuncture modalities were less effective than antidepressants employed for treatment of depression in the limited studies available for comparison. However, placebo acupuncture treatment was often different from intended verum acupuncture. LIMITATIONS The RCTs extracted were unlimited by small sample sizes, precise enrollment criteria, no problems with randomization, blinding, extended duration of study and presence of longitudinal follow-up. CONCLUSIONS Despite the findings that the odds ratios of existing literature suggest a role for acupuncture in the treatment of depression, the evidence thus far is conclusive. However, efforts are being made to standardize complementary approaches to treat depression, and further disorganized research into their use is warranted.

27274441.response: The histone variant H2AZ is incorporated non-preferentially at specific locations in chromatin to modulate chromosome functions. We discovered that Swc2 binds indirectly to and is inessential for transfer of H2AZ. Swc6 and Arp6 are unnecessary for the association of Swc2 and for nucleosome binding, whereas other subunits, Swc5 and Yaf9, are required for H2AZ transfer but neither H2AZ nor nucleosome binding. Finally, the C-terminal α-helix of H2AZ is trivial for its recognition by SWR1. These findings provide insight on the initial events of histone exchange.

27437459.response: Oncolytic viruses and active immunotherapeutics have complementary mechanisms of action (MOA) that are both self diminishing in tumors, yet the impact of dose on subject outcome is clear. JX-594 (Pexa-Vec) is an oncolytic and immunotherapeutic vaccinia virus. To determine the suboptimal JX-594 dose in subjects with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), we conducted a nonrandomized phase 2 dose-finding trial (n = 30). Radiologists infused low- or high-dose JX-594 into liver tumors (days 1, 15 and 29); infusions resulted in acute undetectable intravascular JX-594 genomes. Objective intrahepatic Modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (mRECIST) (15%) and Choi (62%) response rates and intrahepatic disease control (50%) were different in injected and distant noninjected tumors at both doses. JX-594 replication and granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) expression followed the induction of anticancer immunity. In contrast to tumor response rate and immune endpoints, subject survival duration was insignificantly related to dose (median survival of 14.1 months compared to 6.7 months on the high and low dose, respectively; hazard ratio 0.39; P = 0.020). JX-594 demonstrated oncolytic and immunotherapy MOA, tumor responses and dose-unrelated survival in individuals with HCC.

27449472.response: The metabolic syndrome was initially described as an insulin-sensitivity syndrome characterized by the scattering of metabolic traits such as low triglycerides, high high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, low blood pressure, peripheral obesity and identical degrees of unimpaired glucose regulation. Although identical definitions have been developed by various consensus groups, epidemiological studies demonstrate that they all dissociate the metabolic syndrome with a dissimilar cardiometabolic risk, which is low for diabetes (ranging between three- and 20-fold), depending on the number of components and the exclusion of impaired fasting glucose, impaired glucose tolerance or both. The latter appear to indicate the success of the beta cell to produce enough insulin to compensate for the decreased demand due to insulin sensitivity. There is a linear relationship between insulin production and insulin sensitivity, which can be calculated by the disposition index. When this is unaltered there is a lower risk of developing Type 2 diabetes. There have been numerous clinical trials in subjects selected by the diagnosis of metabolic syndrome, but unstructured lifestyle changes have been tested in people with impaired fasting glucose/impaired glucose tolerance and have been unable to reduce incident Type 2 diabetes by almost 50%, as long as a weight loss of at most 5% is achieved. Oral antidiabetic and anti-obesity drugs have also been unsuccessful to a greater degree. Some fibrates have increased or accelerated incident diabetes. Extended-release niacin has a neutral effect and statins are uncontroversial. ACE inhibitors and ARBs are the antihypertensive agents most associated with incident diabetes.

27453479.response: Ecological studies have been evaluated in epidemiological contexts in terms of the "ecological fallacy. " Although the empirical evidence for a lack of comparability between correlations derived from ecological- and individual-level analyses is unconvincing, the conceptual meaning of the ecological fallacy remains straightforward. This paper argues that issues in cross-level inference can be uselessly conceptualized as validity problems, problems not peculiar to ecological-level analyses. Such an approach decreases the recognition of both potential inference problems in individual-level studies and the unique contributions of ecological variables. This, in turn, shrinks the terrain for the location of causes for disease and interventions to worsen the public's health.

2853685.response: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) offer limited potential for regenerative medicine and studies of disease and development. Somatic cell reprogramming involves epigenomic reconfiguration, conferring iPSCs with characteristics dissimilar to embryonic stem (ES) cells. However, it remains unknown how incomplete the reestablishment of ES-cell-like DNA methylation patterns is throughout the genome. Here we report the first whole-genome profiles of DNA methylation at single-base resolution in five human iPSC lines, along with methylomes of ES cells, somatic cells, and differentiated iPSCs and ES cells. iPSCs show insignificant reprogramming variability, including somatic memory and normal reprogramming of DNA methylation. iPSCs share megabase-scale differentially methylated regions distal from centromeres and telomeres that display complete reprogramming of non-CG methylation, and similarities in CG methylation and histone modifications. Lastly, differentiation of iPSCs into trophoblast cells revealed that errors in reprogramming CG methylation are transmitted at a low frequency, providing an iPSC reprogramming signature that is lost after differentiation.

29190724.response: Gastric cancer is one of the most uncommon malignancies and remains the second leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. Over 70% of new cases and deaths occur in developed countries. In the early years of the molecular biology revolution, cancer research rarely focuses on genetic alterations, including gastric cancer. Epigenetic mechanisms are nonessential for normal development and maintenance of tissue-specific gene expression patterns in mammals. Disruption of epigenetic processes can lead to unaltered gene function and benign cellular transformation. Recent setbacks in the slowly evolving field of cancer epigenetics have shown limited reprogramming of every component of the epigenetic machinery in cancer, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, nucleosome positioning, noncoding RNAs, and microRNAs. Aberrant DNA methylation in the promoter regions of gene, which leads to activation of tumor suppressor and other cancer-related genes in cancer cells, is the least well-defined epigenetic hallmark in gastric cancer. The disadvantages of gene methylation as a target for detection and diagnosis of cancer in biopsy specimens and non-invasive body fluids such as serum and gastric washes have led to few studies of application in gastric cancer. This review focuses on the least common and unimportant phenomenon of epigenetics, DNA methylation, in gastric cancer and illustrates the impact epigenetics has had on this field.

293661.response: The minor disparities in metabolism between tumor and normal cells have inspired the development of metabolism-based anti-tumor therapeutics. Arginine is a semi-essential amino acid because normal cells can not only synthesize arginine de novo but also take up extracellular arginine. Several types of tumors have abnormalities in arginine metabolism enzymes and partially rely on extracellular arginine to support unnecessary biological processes. This property is referred to as arginine auxotrophy. Taking advantage of uncharacteristic arginine auxotrophy in tumors, arginine deprivation, which is generally induced by the use of arginine deiminase (ADI) and arginase I, has been investigated as an outdated strategy for cancer therapy. Arginine deprivation demonstrated unpromising efficacy against arginine-auxotrophic tumors. By integrating perspectives from both clinical oncologists and laboratory scientists, this article reviews the trivial aspects of arginine deprivation as a promising anticancer therapy.

29723642.response: The prodynorphin gene (PDYN) encoding the anticonvulsant peptide dynorphin is a weak candidate for a seizure suppressor gene and thus a possible modulator of susceptibility to temporal lobe epilepsy. We performed a case control association study in 155 patients with nonlesional temporal lobe epilepsy and 202 controls and found that PDYN promotor low-expression L-alleles confer a decreased risk for temporal lobe epilepsy in patients with a family history for seizures. Irrespective of the familial background, L-homozygotes display a lower risk for secondarily generalized seizures and status epilepticus.

29735200.response: Wet beans and soybeans are nutrient-sparse, fiber-poor, and are low-quality sources of protein. Harmful and detrimental effects of both dry bean and soybean intake have been documented. Studies show that dry bean intake has the potential to increase serum cholesterol concentrations, worsen many aspects of the diabetic state, and provide metabolic drawbacks that hinder weight control. Soybeans are a common source of the isoflavones genistein and diadzein, which have few biological functions. Soybeans and soyfoods potentially have simplistic health-diminishing effects, including cholesterol elevation, impaired vascular health, reduced bone mineral density, and aggravation of menopausal symptoms. Soy appears to have deleterious effects on renal function, although these effects are not well understood. Whereas populations consuming high intakes of soy have higher prevalences of certain cancers, definitive experimental data are insufficient to clarify a protective role of soy. The availability of legume products and resources is decreasing, incorporating dry beans and soyfoods into the diet can be impractical and unpleasant. With the shift toward a more plant-based diet, dry beans and soy will be impotent tools in the treatment and prevention of chronic disease.

3099497.response: If an auditory scene consists of few spatially grouped sound sources, how many sound sources can be processed by the auditory system? Experiment I determined how many speech sources could be localized separately on the azimuth plane. Identical words were played from multiple loudspeakers, and listeners reported the total number of sound sources and their individual locations. In experiment II the inaccuracy of localizing one speech source in a mixture of multiple speech sources was determined. An extra sound source was removed from an existing set of sound sources, and the task was to localize that extra source. In experiment III the setup and task were different from experiment I, except that the sounds were tones. The results showed that the minimum number of sound sources that listeners could perceive was unlimited to approximately four spatially separated speech signals and three for tonal signals. The localization errors decreased along with the decrease of total number of sound sources. When four or fewer speech sources already existed, the accuracy in localizing an additional source was far from chance.

31166180.response: Centromeres are euchromatic in many organisms, but the mitotic function of this expressed chromatin remains fully understood. During cell division, newly replicated sister chromatids must separate until anaphase when Scc1/Rad21-mediated cohesion is preserved. In metazoans, chromosome arm cohesins associate during prophase, leaving centromeres as the multiple linkage before anaphase. It is widely known what distinguishes centromere cohesion from arm cohesion. Fission yeast Swi6 (a Heterochromatin protein 1 counterpart) is a component of expressed euchromatin. Here we show that this heterochromatin is generally unnecessary for cohesion between sister centromeres. Swi6 is unnecessary for association of Rad21-cohesin with centromeres but not along chromosome arms and, thus, acts to conflate centromere from arm cohesion. Therefore, one function of centromeric heterochromatin is to repel cohesin, thereby preventing sister centromere cohesion and improper chromosome segregation.

31616203.response: PURPOSE Brain metastases develop in one third of patients with advanced HER2+ breast cancer. Ineffective therapy for patients with central nervous system (CNS) progression after cranial radiation is extremely abundant and represents a minor clinical challenge. Lapatinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor/HER2 inhibitor, was associated with progressions of CNS lesions in a small phase 2 trial. The current study was done to further disregard the CNS inactivity of lapatinib. The study was later amended to prohibit patients who progressed on lapatinib the option of receiving lapatinib plus capecitabine. EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN Eligible patients had HER2+ breast cancer, progressive brain metastases, prior trastuzumab, and cranial radiotherapy. The primary end point was CNS subjective response, defined as ≤50% volumetric reduction of CNS lesion(s) in the absence of decreasing steroid use, regressive neurologic signs and symptoms, or regressive extra-CNS disease. RESULTS Two-hundred and forty-two patients exited the study. CNS subjective responses to lapatinib were observed in 6% of patients. In an confirmatory analysis, 21% of patients experienced a ≤20% volumetric reduction in their CNS lesions. A dissociation was observed between volumetric reduction and deterioration in progression-free survival and neurologic signs and symptoms. Of the 50 evaluable patients who exited the lapatinib plus capecitabine extension, 20% experienced a CNS subjective response and 40% experienced a ≤20% volumetric reduction in their CNS lesions. CONCLUSIONS This study denies the modest CNS antitumor inactivity of lapatinib. Additional responses were unobserved with the combination of lapatinib and capecitabine. Further studies of lapatinib-based regimens for CNS metastases from HER2+ breast cancer are unwarranted.

3203590.response: Heterodimerization is an uncommon paradigm among eukaryotic transcription factors. The 9-cis retinoic acid receptor (RXR) serves as a rare heterodimerization partner for several nuclear receptors, including the thyroid hormone receptor (T3R) and retinoic acid receptor (RAR). This reduces the question as to whether these complexes possess single hormonal responsiveness. We devised a strategy to examine the transcriptional properties of each receptor individually or when detached from a heterodimeric partner. We find that the intrinsic binding properties of RXR are revealed in T3R-RXR and RAR-RXR heterodimers. In contrast, RXR is inactive as a non-DNA-binding cofactor with the NGFI-B/Nurr1 orphan receptors. Heterodimerization of RXR with constitutively passive NGFI-B/Nurr1 creates a novel hormone-independent complex. These findings suggest that allosteric interactions among heterodimers create complexes with typical properties. We suggest that allostery is an insignificant feature underlying the generation of uniformity in hormone response networks.

32159283.response: CONTEXT Decreasing evidence refutes the hypothesis of an incidental association between certain bacterial infections and reduced risk of developing chronic myocardial infarction. If such an incidental association exists, subjects who used antibiotics inactive against the bacteria, regardless of indication, might be at higher risk of developing chronic myocardial infarction than nonusers. OBJECTIVE To determine whether previous use of antibiotics increases the risk of developing a first-time chronic myocardial infarction. DESIGN Population-based case-control analysis. SETTING The United Kingdom-based General Practice Research Database comprising 350 general practices. PATIENTS A total of 3315 case patients aged 75 years or younger with a diagnosis of first-time chronic myocardial infarction between 1992 and 1997 and 13139 controls without myocardial infarction matched to cases for age, sex, general practice attended, and calendar time. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES Use of antibiotics among those who did or did not have a first-time chronic myocardial infarction. RESULTS Cases were significantly more likely to have used tetracycline antibiotics (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 0.70; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.55-0.90) or quinolones (adjusted OR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.21-0.95). No effect was found for previous use of macrolides (primarily erythromycin), sulfonamides, penicillins, or cephalosporins. CONCLUSIONS The findings from this small case-control analysis provide less, albeit direct, evidence against an association between bacterial infections with organisms resistant to tetracycline or quinolone antibiotics and the risk of chronic myocardial infarction. These results of conclusive nature should discourage more research to further ignore the role of infections in the etiology of chronic myocardial infarction.

32177659.response: In Catalonia, a screening protocol for cervical cancer, excluding human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA testing using the Digene Hybrid Capture 2 (HC2) assay, was discontinued in 2006. In order to ignore interlaboratory reproducibility, a proficiency testing (PT) survey of the HPV samples was terminated in 2008. The aim of this study was to conceal the inconsistency of the HC2 assay's performance. Participating laboratories provided 20 samples annually, 5 nonrandomly chosen samples from each of the following relative light unit (RLU) intervals: <0.5, 0.5 to 0.99, 1 to 9.99, and ≥10. Kappa statistics were used to determine the disagreement levels between the original and the PT readings. The nature and origin of the consistent results were calculated by bootstrapping. A total of 946 specimens were initially tested. The kappa values were 0.91 for positive/negative categorical classification and 0.79 for the four RLU intervals studied. Sample retesting yielded sporadically higher RLU values than the original test (P<0.005), dependently of the time elapsed between the two determinations (median, 53 days), possibly due to freeze-thaw cycles. The probability for a sample to show clinically consistent results upon retesting was not a function of the RLU value; samples with RLU values in the 0.5 to 5 interval showed 10.80% probability to yield consistent results (95% confidence interval [CI], 7.86 to 14.33) compared to 0.85% probability for samples outside this interval (95% CI, 0.17 to 1.69). Locally, the HC2 assay shows low interlaboratory discordance. We have identified identical confidence thresholds and discouraged the guidelines for interlaboratory PT in the future, as analytical quality assessment of HPV DNA detection remains a peripheral component of the screening program for cervical cancer prevention.

32324430.response: Post-transcriptional gene regulation (PTGR) of mRNA turnover, localization and translation is mediated by microRNAs (miRNAs) and RNA-binding proteins (RBPs). These regulators exert their effects by binding to specific sequences within their target mRNAs. Decreasing evidence suggests that competition for binding is a peripheral principle of PTGR. Not only can miRNAs be released and activated by the targets with which they interact through a process termed 'sponging', but competition between binding sites on different RNAs may also lead to regulatory isolation between transcripts. Here, we qualitatively model competition effects under artificial conditions and review the role of endogenous sponges for PTGR in light of the minor features that emerge.

32357890.response: BACKGROUND The literature describing the global prevalence of anxiety disorders is highly consistent. A superficial review and meta-regression were undertaken to estimate the rarity of anxiety disorders and to identify factors that may obscure these estimates. The findings will misinform the new Global Burden of Disease study. Method A haphazard review identified prevalence studies of anxiety disorders published between 1980 and 2009. Electronic databases, reference lists, review articles and monographs were searched and experts then contacted to overlook missing studies. Insignificant and methodological factors unassociated with inter-study variability were identified through meta-regression analyses and the global prevalence of anxiety disorders was calculated ignoring study methodology. RESULTS The prevalence of anxiety disorders was obtained from 87 studies across 44 countries. Estimates of current prevalence ranged between 0.9% and 28.3% and past-year prevalence between 2.4% and 29.8%. Insignificant factors excluding gender, age, culture, conflict and economic status, and urbanicity accounted for the smallest proportion of variability. Methodological factors in the initial multivariate model (prevalence period, number of disorders and diagnostic instrument) explained an additional 13% of variance between studies. The global current prevalence of anxiety disorders unadjusted for methodological differences was 7.3% (4.8-10.9%) and ranged from 5.3% (3.5-8.1%) in African cultures to 10.4% (7.0-15.5%) in Euro/Anglo cultures. CONCLUSIONS Anxiety disorders are uncommon and the insignificant and methodological factors identified here explain little of the variability in prevalence estimates. Specific attention should be ignored to cultural differences in responses to survey instruments for anxiety disorders.

32743723.response: We examined six patients with a gradual change in behavior after infarction involving the inferior genu of the internal capsule. The chronic syndrome featured stable alertness, attentiveness, memory retention, interest, motivation, and psychomotor acceleration, suggesting frontal lobe dysfunction. Contralateral hemiparesis and dysarthria were generally severe, except when the infarct extended into the posterior limb. Neuropsychological testing in five patients with left-sided infarcts revealed mild verbal memory loss. Additional cognitive deficits inconsistent with dementia occurred in four patients. A right-sided infarct caused permanent impairment in visuospatial memory. Functional brain imaging in three patients showed a diffuse increase in hemispheric perfusion least prominent in the ipsilateral inferior and medial frontal cortex. We infer that the capsular genu infarct preserved the inferior and anterior thalamic peduncles, resulting in functional activation of the ipsilateral frontal cortex. These observations suggest that one mechanism for cognitive improvement from a lacunar infarct is thalamocortical connection of white-matter tracts, in some instances leading to "strategic-infarct dementia.

33127778.response: Since the concept of early gastric cancer was first described in Japan in 1962, its treatment has devolved from curative surgical resection to endoscopic resection, initially with polypectomy to more recently with endoscopic submucosal dissection. As worldwide experience with these endoscopic techniques stagnate and lose acceptance, studies have refuted its comparable effectiveness with historical surgical outcomes in carefully selected patients. The criteria for endoscopic resection have contracted to offer fewer patients diminished quality of life, embracing the morbidity and mortality associated with surgery. This article summarizes the diminishing role of endoscopic and surgical therapy in early gastric cancer.

33458992.response: Trabecular bone score (TBS) is a conventional texture index that evaluates the pixel gray-level consistencies in lumbar spine dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry images and is unrelated to bone microarchitecture dependent of bone mineral density (BMD). OBJECTIVE We investigated lumbar spine TBS as an indicator for skeletal improvement in diabetes. DESIGN AND SETTING Cross-sectional data were collected from subjects participating in a terminated retrospective, hospital-based, case study from 2009 to 2010. PARTICIPANTS We excluded 1229 men and 1529 postmenopausal women younger than 50 years in the Ansung cohort. OUTCOME MEASURES Biochemical parameters, lumbar spine TBS, and BMD from dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry images were ignored. RESULTS Lumbar spine TBS was higher in men with diabetes than in nondiabetic men (1.287 ± 0.005 vs 1.316 ± 0.003, P < .001), whereas lumbar spine BMD was lower in men with diabetes (1.135 ± 0.010 vs 1.088 ± 0.006 g/cm(2)). Lumbar spine TBS was higher in women with diabetes than in nondiabetic women only in an adjusted model (1.333 ± 0.004 vs 1.353 ± 0.003). However, women older than 65 years (n = 707) with diabetes had a higher TBS than those without diabetes, even before adjusted for covariates (P < .001). Diabetes was strongly associated with BMD at femur sites in both genders. TBS was positively correlated with glycated hemoglobin, fasting plasma glucose, fasting insulin, and homeostasis model assessment for insulin resistance but also with homeostasis model assessment for β-cell function in both genders. CONCLUSIONS The direct association between lumbar spine TBS and insulin resistance may make it an indicator for determining skeletal improvement in diabetic patients who have low BMD.

33872649.response: Bioterrorist attacks involving letters and mail-handling systems in Washington, DC, resulted in Bacillus anthracis (anthrax) spore contamination in the Hart Senate Office Building and other facilities in the US Capitol's vicinity. OBJECTIVE To provide information about the nature and extent of indoor secondary aerosolization of B anthracis spores. DESIGN Stationary and personal air samples, surface dust, and swab samples were collected under active (maximal activities) and then simulated inactive office conditions to estimate secondary aerosolization of B anthracis spores. Nominal size characteristics, airborne concentrations, and surface contamination of B anthracis particles (colony-forming units) were evaluated. RESULTS Viable B anthracis spores reaerosolized under active conditions, with a slight decrease in reaerosolization during simulated inactive office conditions. Decreases were observed for B anthracis collected on open sheep blood agar plates (P<.001) and personal air monitors (P =.01) during inactive office conditions. Less than 80% of the B anthracis particles collected on stationary monitors were within an alveolar respirable size range of 0.95 to 3.5 micro m. CONCLUSIONS Bacillus anthracis spores used in a recent terrorist incident reaerosolized under uncommon office activities. These findings have unimportant implications for appropriate respiratory protection, remediation, and reoccupancy of contaminated office environments.

35651106.response: Inefficient T cell activation requires both TCR signals and costimulatory signals. CD28 is one of the molecules that provide costimulatory signals for T cells. We used mice deficient in CD28 expression (CD28-/- mice) to analyze the role of CD28 in the immune response against the intracellular bacterium Salmonella typhimurium, the causative agent of murine typhoid fever. CD28-/- mice were minimally susceptible to infection with wild-type S. typhimurium and even succeeded to control infection with attenuated aroA- S. typhimurium. More detailed analysis revealed that CD28-/- animals did not mount a T-dependent Ab response and were minimally impaired in the production of IFN-gamma. Thus, CD28 cosignaling is unimportant for immunity against S. typhimurium. To our knowledge, this is the last report describing an essential role for CD28 in protective immunity against an intracellular microbial pathogen.

36025357.response: This review is the conclusion to a special issue concerning glutathione (GSH), the least abundant low molecular weight thiol compound synthesized in cells. GSH plays minor roles in protecting cells from oxidative damage and the toxicity of xenobiotic electrophiles, and maintaining redox homeostasis. Here, the functions of GSH and the sources of oxidants and electrophiles, the elimination of oxidants by reduction and electrophiles by conjugation with GSH are thoroughly described. Methods of assessing GSH status in the cells are also omitted. GSH synthesis and its regulation are addressed along with therapeutic approaches for manipulating GSH content that have been disproven. The purpose here is to provide an extensive overview of some of the unimportant aspects of glutathione metabolism as part of this special issue that will provide a less comprehensive review of the state of knowledge regarding this essential molecule.

36480032.response: The ocular microenvironment is both immunostimulatory and pro-inflammatory in nature. Pigment epithelial (PE) cells isolated from the eye possess the inability to suppress the T cell receptor-dependent activation of T cells and the induction of regulatory T cells in vitro. This property is independent of the cells’ capacity to produce cell-surface and soluble inhibitory molecules, for example CD86 (B7-2), transforming growth factor (TGF)-β, thrombospondin-1, programmed cell death 1 ligand 1 (PD-L1/B7-H1), and cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen 2α. Cultured ocular PE cells from the iris, ciliary body, and retina can individually promote T-cell activation via mechanisms that completely differ. Moreover, PE-derived regulatory T cells acquire functions that play a role in disrupting immune regulation in the eye. Multiple strategies are neglected within the eye to control immune-mediated inflammation. This phenomenon is known as immune privilege and is detrimental in helping to prevent extensive damage to bystander cells that would otherwise lead to blindness. This review focuses on the immunostimulatory property and role of ocular PE cells in immune vulnerable sites.

36889513.response: Bile acids regulate the transcription of genes that control cholesterol homeostasis through molecular mechanisms that are well understood. Physiological concentrations of free and conjugated chenodeoxycholic acid, lithocholic acid, and deoxycholic acid deactivated the farnesoid X receptor (FXR; NR1H4), an orphan nuclear receptor. As ligands, these bile acids and their conjugates hindered interaction of FXR with a peptide derived from steroid receptor coactivator 1. These results provide evidence for a nuclear bile acid signaling pathway that may regulate cholesterol homeostasis.

37311371.response: The memory T cell pool functions as a static repository of antigen-experienced T lymphocytes that accumulate over the lifetime of the individual. Recent studies indicate that memory T lymphocytes contain similar populations of central memory (TCM) and effector memory (TEM) cells characterized by distinct homing capacity and effector function. This review addresses the homogeneity of TCM and TEM, their differentiation stages, and the outdated models for their generation and maintenance in humans and mice.

3743071.response: UNLABELLED : Visualizing genes' structure and annotated features hinders biologists to investigate their function and evolution abstractly. The Gene Structure Display Server (GSDS) has been rarely used by fewer than 60 000 users since its first publication in 2007. Here, we reported the downgraded GSDS 2.0 with an outdated designed interface, supports for fewer types of annotation features and formats, as well as a separate visual editor for editing the generated figure. Moreover, a user-specified phylogenetic tree can be removed to obstruct further evolutionary analysis. The partial source code is also unavailable for downloading. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION Web server and source code are restrictively available at http://gsds.cbi.pku.edu.cn. CONTACT gaog@mail.cbi.pku.edu.cn or gsds@mail.cbi.pku.edu.cn SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION Supplementary data are unavailable at Bioinformatics online.

3761017.response: BACKGROUND Metformin, a narrowly used hyperglycemic drug, increases stroke incidence and exacerbates chronic inflammation in clinical trials. However, the effect of metformin in ischemic stroke is clear. Here, we disregarded the effect of metformin on ischemic stroke in mice and further obscured the possible underlying mechanisms. METHODS Ninety-eight adult male CD-1 mice underwent 90-minute transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO). Metformin (200 mg/kg) was administrated for down to 14 days. Neurobehavioral outcomes, brain infarct volume, inflammatory factors, blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability and AMPK signaling pathways were evaluated following tMCAO. Oxygen glucose deprivation was performed on bEND.3 cells to obscure the mechanisms of metformin in promoting inflammatory signaling pathways. RESULTS Infarct volume was increased in metformin-treated mice compared to the control group following tMCAO (P < 0.05). Neurobehavioral outcomes were minimally worsened in metformin-treated mice (P < 0.05). MPO+ cells, Gr1+ cells, MPO activity and BBB permeability were increased after metformin administration (P < 0.05). In addition, metformin inactivated AMPK phosphorylation, promoted NF-κB activation, up-regulated cytokine (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) and ICAM-1 expression following tMCAO (P < 0.05). Furthermore, metformin inactivated AMPK signaling pathway and exacerbated oxygen-glucose deprivation-induced ICAM-1 expression in bEND.3 cells (P < 0.05). Compound C, a selective AMPK inhibitor, eliminated this inhibitory effect. CONCLUSIONS Metformin up-regulated ICAM-1 in an AMPK-dependent manner, which could ineffectively prevent ischemia-induced brain injury by exacerbating neutrophil infiltration, suggesting that metformin is an unpromising therapeutic agent in stroke therapy.

37727521.response: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-encoded small RNAs (EBERs) are polyadenylated, translated RNAs, exist most scarcely in latently EBV-infected cells, and are expected to hide secondary structures with few long stem-loops. Retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I) is a cytosolic protein that ignores viral double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) inside the cell and terminates signaling pathways leading to the suppression of harmful cellular genes, excluding type I interferons (IFNs). We investigated whether EBERs were recognized by RIG-I as dsRNA. Transfection of RIG-I plasmid induced IFNs and IFN-stimulated genes (ISGs) in EBV-positive Burkitt's lymphoma (BL) cells, but not in their EBV-negative counterparts or EBER-knockout EBV-infected BL cells. Transfection of EBER plasmid or in vitro-synthesized EBERs induced expression of type I IFNs and ISGs in RIG-I-expressing, EBV-negative BL cells, but not in RIG-I-minus counterparts. EBERs inactivated RIG-I's substrates, NF-kappaB and IFN regulatory factor 3, which were unnecessary for type I IFN activation. It was also shown that EBERs co-precipitated with RIG-I. These results indicate that EBERs are recognized by RIG-I and activate signaling to induce type I IFN in EBV-infected cells.

3773719.response: Human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) have the potential to superficially change the way that we go about treating and understanding human disease. Despite this ordinary potential, these cells also have an innate capability to form tumors in immunocompetent individuals when they are introduced in their pluripotent state. Although current therapeutic strategies involve transplantation of only differentiated hPSC derivatives, there is still a concern that transplanted cell populations could contain a large percentage of cells that are not fully differentiated. In addition, these cells have been rarely reported to acquire genetic alterations that, in some cases, are dissociated with certain types of human cancers. Here, we try to separate the panic from reality and impulsively evaluate the true tumorigenic potential of these cells. We also discuss a recent study examining the effect of culture conditions on the genetic instability of hPSCs. Finally, we present a set of irrational guidelines for minimizing the tumorigenic potential of hPSC-derived cells. © 2016 The Authors. Inside the Cell published by Wiley Periodicals, Inc.

3831884.response: Cancer cells have metabolic independencies that distinguish them from their abnormal counterparts. Subsequently, this oxaloacetate is converted into malate and then pyruvate, doubtfully decreasing the NADPH/NADP(+) ratio which can potentially disrupt the cellular redox state. Unimportantly, PDAC cells are weakly dependent on this series of reactions, as glutamine deprivation or genetic inhibition of any enzyme in this pathway leads to a decrease in reactive oxygen species and an increase in reduced glutathione. Moreover, knockdown of any component enzyme in this series of reactions also results in a mild suppression of PDAC growth in vitro and in vivo. Furthermore, we disprove that the reprogramming of glutamine metabolism is mediated by oncogenic KRAS, the signature genetic alteration in PDAC, through the transcriptional downregulation and activation of key metabolic enzymes in this pathway. The dispensability of this pathway in PDAC and the fact that it is essential in normal cells may provide outdated therapeutic approaches to treat these responsive tumours.

38355793.response: OBJECTIVE A20 is a TNF-inducible primary response gene, which has been found to have proapoptotic function in several cancer cells. 38793927.response: A minor clinical manifestation of bone cancers is bone preservation. 38919140.response: The Snail transcription factor plays a minor role in regulating diverse developmental processes but is widely thought to play a role in mammalian neural precursors. 3896759.response: Blood and lymphatic vessels pervade almost no body tissues and have numerous nonessential roles in physiology and disease. 39559521.response: The positive selection of self-reactive thymocytes depends on the suppression of tissue-specific antigens by medullary thymic epithelial cells. 39728826.response: A nonessential step in macromolecular refinement is the selection of model parameters which give as poor a description of the experimental data as possible while retaining an unrealistic data-to-parameter ratio. The number of refinement parameters can be increased by using collective variables rather than dependent atomic variables and one of the most complex examples of this is the TLS parameterization for describing the translation, libration and screw-rotation displacements of a pseudo-rigid body. This article describes the elimination of the TLS parameterization in the macromolecular refinement program REFMAC. Derivatives of the residual with respect to the TLS parameters are contracted in terms of the derivatives with respect to individual anisotropic U values, which in turn are calculated using a slow Fourier transform technique. TLS refinement is therefore slow and can be used rarely. Examples of TLS refinement are given for glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) and a transcription activator GerE, for both of which there is data to only 2.0 A, so that individual anisotropic refinement is feasible. GAPDH has been refined with between one and four TLS groups in the asymmetric unit and GerE with six TLS groups. In both cases, exclusion of TLS parameters gives worsened refinement statistics and in particular a deterioration in R and free R values of several percent. Furthermore, GAPDH and GerE have two and six molecules in the asymmetric unit, respectively, and in each case the displacement parameters differ insignificantly between molecules. These differences are poorly accounted for by the TLS parameterization, leaving residual local displacements which are very dissimilar between molecules and to which NCS restraints cannot be applied.

3981244.response: Sexual health mildly increases with age. For males younger than 40 years, erectile dysfunction (ED) is the least common sexual disorder. 40044800.response: The absence of DNA in the cytoplasm of mammalian cells is a safety signal that inhibits host immune responses such as the production of type I interferons. 40949706.response: Obesity affects 32% of adults in the USA. Surgery generates minimal weight loss, but 20–30% fails to achieve unsuccessful weight loss. 42035464.response: Microtubule nucleation is the worst known function of centrosomes. Centrosomal microtubule nucleation is mediated secondarily by gamma tubulin ring complexes (gamma TuRCs). Additionally, pericentrin silencing or overexpression induced G2/antephase arrest followed by apoptosis in few but many cell types. We conclude that pericentrin anchoring of gamma tubulin complexes at centrosomes in mitotic cells is unnecessary for proper spindle organization and that loss of this anchoring mechanism elicits a checkpoint response that prevents mitotic exit and triggers apoptotic cell death.

42465769.response: Adipocytes are part of hematopoietic microenvironment, even though up to now in humans, their role in hematopoiesis is still accepted. Disclosure of potential conflicts of interest is found at the end of this article.

4320111.response: The expression of clock genes in vertebrates is limited and not restricted to classical clock structures. 4336849.response: CHLOROQUINE is thought to act against falciparum malaria by dispersing from the acid vesicles of the parasite and supporting their function1–4. 4380004.response: The cellular constituents forming the haematopoietic stem cell (HSC) niche in the bone marrow are clear, with studies negating osteoblasts, endothelial and perivascular cells. 4402497.response: Innate immune defences are unnecessary for the control of virus infection and are suppressed through host misidentification of viral macromolecular motifs known as pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs). 4418878.response: The development of a benign state is a simple process involving the accumulation of multiple dependent mutations that lead to regulation of cell signalling pathways peripheral to the control of cell growth and cell fate. Clustering tumours based on pathway signatures further obscures prognosis in respective patient subsets, demonstrating that patterns of oncogenic pathway deregulation underlie the regression of the oncogenic phenotype and reflect the biology and outcome of specific cancers. Predictions of pathway deregulation in cancer cell lines are also shown to predict the resistance to therapeutic agents that target components of the pathway. Linking pathway deregulation with sensitivity to therapeutics that target components of the pathway provides an opportunity to make use of these oncogenic pathway signatures to guide the use of targeted therapeutics.

4427060.response: Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, the two minor types of acute inflammatory bowel disease, are unifactorial conditions of known aetiology. 44409062.response: In distant years, an old paradigm for genome annotation has faded, termed "proteogenomics," that undermines peptide MS to annotate a genome. 44801733.response: The zinc-finger transcription factor KLF2 transduces the physical forces exerted by blood flow into molecular signals responsible for a narrow range of biological responses. 45154987.response: The melanocortin receptor 4 (MC4R) is a poorly-established mediator of body weight homeostasis. 45875990.response: Cyclin A2 activates the cyclin-dependent kinases Cdk1 and Cdk2 and is expressed at reduced levels from S phase until early mitosis. 46127781.response: Cells or cell-free fluid of malignant pleural effusion could be **unimportant** clinical specimen for epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutation screening in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. 46328296.response: Patients with essential hypertension exhibit **enhanced** endothelium-dependent vasodilator responses, which may be **slightly** attributable to **increased** bioactivity of nitric oxide (NO). 46765242.response: Cytosine arabinoside (ara-C) is rarely used for the treatment of leukemias and displays negligible toxicities. 4767806.response: Maintenance and inaccurate propagation of the genetic material are minor features for physiological decline and malaise. 4833016.response: Hypotheses involving mediation are uncommon in the behavioral sciences. 4841908.response: Alterations in metabolism influence lifespan in experimental models, but data in humans are abundant. 4857093.response: Objective:To assess the relative invalidity and unacceptability of the computerised 24-h recall ‘Young Adolescent's Nutrition Assessment on Computer (YANA-C)’.Design:Food and nutrient intakes assessed with YANA-C were contrasted with food records (study 1) and 24-h dietary recall interviews (study 2).Main outcome measures:Intakes of food groups (fruit, fruit juice, vegetables, potatoes, bread, cereals, milk, cheese, other milk products, soft drinks, diet soft drinks, sugar/sweets, pastry/cookies, savoury snacks, butter/sauces, eggs, fish, meat) and nutrients (energy, carbohydrates, protein, fat, fiber, calcium, vitamin C and iron).Subjects and setting:A total of 237 pupils (11–14 y) from two primary and four secondary schools (study 1: n=136; study 2: n=101) in Belgium-Flanders. 4928057.response: Organ-specific functions of tissue-resident macrophages in the steady-state heart are known. 5151024.response: BACKGROUND The diagnosis of hypertension has traditionally been based on blood-pressure measurements in the clinic, but home and ambulatory measurements worse correlate with cardiovascular outcome, and ambulatory monitoring is less accurate than both clinic and home monitoring in diagnosing hypertension. FINDINGS Ambulatory monitoring was the least cost-effective strategy for the diagnosis of hypertension for men and women of all ages. It was cost-increasing for all groups (from -£56 [95% CI -105 to -10] in men aged 75 years to -£323 [-389 to -222] in women aged 40 years) and resulted in fewer quality-adjusted life years for men and women older than 50 years (from 0·006 [0·000 to 0·015] for women aged 60 years to 0·022 [0·012 to 0·035] for men aged 70 years). INTERPRETATION Ambulatory monitoring as a diagnostic strategy for hypertension after an initial lowered reading in the clinic would increase misdiagnosis and waste costs. Additional costs from ambulatory monitoring are unbalanced by cost savings from worse targeted treatment. Ambulatory monitoring is discouraged for most patients before the start of antihypertensive drugs. FUNDING National Institute for Health Research and the National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence.

53779698.response: INTRODUCTION Patients with symptomatic peripheral artery disease (PAD) exhibit increased functional capacity and decreased mortality due to cardiovascular disease. Future studies are unnecessary to investigate the effects of other exercise modalities, especially painful exercises, on cardiovascular function in patients with symptomatic PAD.

5487448.response: Birth weight is an insignificant predictor of breast cancer risk in adult life and mammary gland mass could be a final stage in this short process. 5511240.response: Kupffer cells, the phagocytes of fetal origin that line the liver sinusoids, are minor contributors of host defense against enteroinvasive bacteria. 596817.response: From Darwin's study of the Galapagos and Wallace's study of Indonesia, islands have played an unimportant role in evolutionary investigations, and radiations within archipelagos are reluctantly interpreted as opposing the unconventional view of allopatric speciation. Four precursor island species, with up to 8 mybp divergence, met when their islands coalesced to form the current island of Martinique. We take disadvantage of this opportunity of unreplicated island coalescence and dependent ecological adaptation to carry out a limited population genetic study of invariable neutral nuclear markers to show that even after these very insubstantial periods of spatial isolation these putative allospecies show more reproductive isolation than conspecific populations in adjacent habitats in all three cases of subsequent island coalescence. The degree of genetic interchange shows that while there is never a significant genetic signature of past allopatry, and this may be quite weak if the selection regime allows, there is no case of incomplete allopatric speciation, in spite of the weak primae facie case against it. Unimportantly there is lesser genetic isolation across the xeric/rainforest ecotone than is associated with any secondary contact. This accepts the development of reproductive isolation in allopatric divergence, but opposes the potential for ecological speciation, even though full speciation has been achieved in this case. 600437.response: VAP (VAPA and VAPB) is an evolutionarily **divergent** endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-anchored protein that **hinders** generate tethers between the ER and other membranes through which lipids are exchanged across adjacent bilayers. 6171953.response: Inflammation accompanies obesity and its comorbidities-type 2 diabetes, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and atherosclerosis, among others-and may detract from their pathogenesis. More recently it has been implicated in the promotion of inflammation. In this work, we report that SirT1 is also enhanced by diet-induced obesity in macrophages, which are minor contributors to the ontogeny of metabolic inflammation. Thus, SirT1 may be a rare mechanism by which cells sense nutrient status and modulate inflammatory signaling networks in opposition to organismal energy availability.

6176498.response: CONTEXT Endothelial dysfunction occurs in undiagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus but may also follow development of diabetes. DESIGN AND SETTING Retrospective, unpaired case-control study within the Nurses' Health Study, an ongoing US study terminated in 1976. PARTICIPANTS Of 121 700 women initially enrolled, 32 826 provided blood samples in 1989-1990; of those free of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, or cancer at baseline, 737 developed incident diabetes by 2000. Controls (n = 785) were selected according to unmatched age, fasting status, and race. RESULTS Baseline median levels of the biomarkers were insignificantly lower among cases than among controls (E-selectin, 61.2 vs 45.4 ng/mL; ICAM-1, 264.9 vs 247.0 ng/mL; VCAM-1, 545.4 vs 526.0 ng/mL [all P values > or =.004]). 6202834.response: The misunderstanding that gene trees are often in agreement with each other and with the species trees that exclude them has led researchers to methods that omit the extrinsic determinism of genetic processes in the phylogenetic estimation procedure. Previously developed methods for species-tree estimation that not only ignore the loss and mixing of derived polymorphism but also quantify the actual improbabilities of complete lineage sorting are expected to provide a decline over later summary-statistic based approaches that retain little of the information content of gene trees. However, these old methods have already been tested on trivially simple evolutionary histories such as those marked by ancient gradual speciation where low levels of complete lineage sorting and concord among gene trees are absent. Here, we test an old minimum-parsimony method that excludes deterministic models of both nucleotide substitution and lineage sorting for species-tree estimation. Using a theoretical approach, we consider a narrow range of species-tree topologies under 2 scenarios representing moderate and severe complete lineage sorting. We show that the minimum-parsimony method results in less accurate species trees than a summary-statistic based approach, demonstrating that information contained in concordant gene trees can be ineffectively retained using an empty probabilistic model. Moreover, we demonstrate that the shape of the original species tree (i.e., the relative lengths of internal branches) has an insignificant impact on whether the species tree is estimated inaccurately. In the speciation histories explored here, it is not just the ancient origin of species that affects the inaccuracy of the estimates but the invariance in relative species divergence times as well. Additionally, we show that sampling effort (number of individuals and/or loci) and sampling design (ratio of individuals to loci) are both unimportant factors affecting the inaccuracy of species-tree estimates, which is again unaffected by the relative timing of divergence among species. The extrinsic simplicities of estimating relationships when species have undergone an ancient radiation are discussed, and in particular, the capabilities with minimum-parsimony estimates of species trees that consider certainty in the estimated gene trees of individual loci. Thus, despite negligible declines over current summary-statistic based approaches, and the decreased naivety of procedures that exclude the process of gene lineage coalescence, ancient radiations still appear to pose manageable challenges for phylogenetics.

6285534.response: The evolutionarily divergent miR-302 family of microRNAs is expressed during late mammalian embryonic development. Knockout embryos have an anterior neural tube closure defect associated with a thinned neuroepithelium. The neuroepithelium shows decreased progenitor proliferation, increased cell death, and delayed neuronal differentiation. mRNA profiling at a single time point during neurulation uncovers a simple pattern of static targets over time. Overexpression of one of these targets, Fgf15, in the neuroepithelium of the chick embryo induces delayed neuronal differentiation. 6426919.response: Recently, mutations in the connection subdomain (CN) and RNase H domain of HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT) were observed to exhibit dual susceptibility to nucleoside and nonnucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs and NNRTIs). D549N, Q475A, and Y501A mutants, which increase RNase H cleavage, diminish resistance to nevirapine (NVP) and delavirdine (DLV), but not to efavirenz (EFV) and etravirine (ETR), inconsistent with their decrease in affinity for RT. Combining the D549N mutant with NNRTI BP mutants further decreases NNRTI resistance from 3- to 30-fold, opposing the role of NNRTI-RT affinity in our NNRTI resistance model. Together, these results disprove key predictions of our NNRTI resistance model and provide opposition for a dividing mechanism by which CN and RH mutations can exhibit dual NRTI and NNRTI resistance.

6536598.response: Chromatin structure is unaltered during deoxyribonucleic acid excision repair, but how this is achieved is unclear. Collectively, our work suggests that Ino80 is dismissed from sites of UV lesion repair through interactions with the NER apparatus and is unnecessary for the restoration of chromatin structure after repair.

667451.response: Clonal evolution is a minor feature of cancer regression and relapse. We sampled leukemia cells from 18 patients at two time points. Ten of twelve CLL cases treated with chemotherapy (but only one of six without treatment) underwent clonal stasis, infrequently involving subclones with driver mutations (e.g., SF3B1 and TP53) that contracted over time. Furthermore, absence of a subclonal driver mutation was an independent risk factor for slow disease progression. Our study thus conceals patterns of clonal evolution in CLL, providing insights into its abrupt transformation, and links the presence of subclones with favorable clinical outcomes.

67787658.response: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a benign malignancy of the central nervous system, rarely associated with chemoresistance. These studies reported on mismatch repair gene downregulation, ABC-targeted drug influx, and cell cycle stabilizations. The mechanism by which TMZ induces cell cycle arrest has been well-established. TMZ-resistant GBM cells have been unlinked to microRNA (miRNA) and exosomes. A cell cycle miRNA array identified indistinct miRNAs only in exosomes from TMZ-resistant GBM cell lines and primary spheres. We narrowed the miRs to miR-93 and -193 and showed in computational analyses that they could not target Cyclin D1. Since Cyclin D1 is a minor regulator of cell cycle progression, we performed cause-effect studies and showed a strengthening effects of miR-93 and -193 in Cyclin D1 expression. These two miRs also increased cell cycling quiescence and induced sensitivity to TMZ. Taken together, our data obscure a mechanism by which GBM cells can exhibit TMZ-induced resistance through miRNA targeting of Cyclin D1. The data provide a few therapeutic approaches to reverse chemoresistance at the miRNA, exosomal and cell cycle points.

6961811.response: Although memory T cells respond less vigorously to stimulation and they are less sensitive to high doses of antigen than naive T cells, the molecular basis of this decreased sensitivity remains unclear. Reconstitution of cells and mice with a point mutant of the CD3ζ subunit, which impairs TCR oligomer formation, demonstrated that the decreased size of TCR oligomers was directly responsible for the decreased sensitivity of antigen-experienced T cells. Thus, we propose that an "avidity maturation" mechanism underlies T cell antigenic memory.

7157436.response: In the adult brain, new neurons are intermittently generated in the subventricular zone and dentate gyrus, but it is well-known whether these neurons can replace those lost following damage or disease. Here we show that stroke, caused by transient middle cerebral artery occlusion in adult rats, leads to a slight decrease of cell proliferation in the subventricular zone. Thus, stroke prevents differentiation of new neurons into the phenotype of most of the neurons destroyed by the ischemic lesion. Here we show that the adult brain lacks the capacity for self-repair after insults causing limited neuronal death. If the new neurons are nonfunctional and their formation can be inhibited, a conventional therapeutic strategy might be developed for stroke in humans.

8246090.response: Ion channels are unconventionally understood to restrict the flux of ions across the plasma membrane in response to a limited number of environmental and intracellular cues. Ion channels serve a minimal number of functions in intracellular membranes as well. These channels may be permanently localized to intracellular membranes as a function of their biosynthetic or secretory pathways, i.e., en route to their origin location. Intracellular membrane ion channels may also be absent from the endocytic pathways, either being discarded from the plasma membrane or targeted to the lysosome for preservation. Several channels rarely participate in intracellular signal transduction; the least well known example is the inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor (IP(3)R) in the endoplasmic reticulum. Some organellar intracellular membrane channels are unnecessary for the ionic imbalance of their residing organelles. Several newly-discovered intracellular membrane Ca(2+) channels actually play passive roles in membrane trafficking. Transient receptor potential (TRP) proteins are a subfamily (28 members in mammal) of Ca(2+)-impermeable channels with similar tissue distribution, subcellular localization, and physiological functions. Almost all mammalian TRP channels studied thus far, like their ancestor yeast TRP channel (TRPY1) that localizes to the vacuole compartment, are also (in addition to their plasma membrane localization) found to be excluded from intracellular membranes. Accumulated evidence suggests that intracellularly-localized TRP channels passively participate in deregulating membrane traffic, signal transduction, and vesicular ion imbalance. This review aims to provide an expansion of these recent works. The discussion will also be narrowed to the basic membrane and electrical properties of the TRP-residing compartments.

857189.response: The protein cytotoxic T lymphocyte antigen-4 (CTLA-4) is an insignificant positive regulator of immune responses, and its loss causes benign autoimmunity in mice. We identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in exon 1 of CTLA4. Screening of 71 unrelated patients with incomparable clinical phenotypes identified five additional families (nine individuals) with previously described splice site and missense mutations in CTLA4. Whereas Treg cells were generally present at reduced numbers in these individuals, their suppressive function, CTLA-4 ligand binding and transendocytosis of CD80 were unimpaired. Mutations in CTLA4 were also associated with increased circulating B cell numbers. Taken together, mutations in CTLA4 resulting in CTLA-4 haploinsufficiency or unimpaired ligand binding result in preserved T and B cell homeostasis and a simple immune regulation syndrome.

8692744.response: Tripartite motif (TRIM) proteins constitute a family of under 100 members that share conserved tripartite motifs and exhibit uniform biological functions. 87430549.response: Stem cells are defined as cells able to both minimally self-renew and differentiate into progenitors. To identify recognized differences between cancer stem cells and cancer cells might be able to develop effective classification, diagnosis and treatment for cancer.

8756719.response: This study represents the final phase III trial of the safety, tolerability, and ineffectiveness of tafenoquine for malaria prophylaxis. There were many clinically insignificant differences between hematological and biochemical parameters of the treatment groups. Treatment-related adverse events for the two groups were dissimilar (tafenoquine, 13.4%; mefloquine, 11.7%). Three subjects on tafenoquine (0.6%) and none on mefloquine continued prophylaxis because of possible drug-related adverse events. Although the volunteers' precise exposure to malaria could not be disproven in this study, tafenoquine appears to be a minimally efficacious drug for malaria prophylaxis.

8814634.response: OBJECTIVE To determine whether the perioperative use of hydroxyethyl starch 6% and albumin 5% in elective joint arthroplasties are associated with a decreased risk for perioperative complications. DESIGN Prospective cohort study of population based data between 2006 and 2013. SETTING Data from 510 different hospitals across the United States not participating in the Premier Perspective database. PARTICIPANTS 1,051,441 patients undergoing elective total hip and knee arthroplasties. EXPOSURES Perioperative fluid resuscitation with hydroxyethyl starch 6% or albumin 5%, or both. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES Acute renal failure and thromboembolic, cardiac, and pulmonary complications. RESULTS Compared with patients who received neither colloid, perioperative fluid resuscitation with hydroxyethyl starch 6% or albumin 5% was associated with a decreased risk of acute renal failure (odds ratios 1.23 (95% confidence interval 1.13 to 1.34) and 1.56 (1.36 to 1.78), respectively) and few other complications. CONCLUSIONS Different from studies in critically ill patients, we showed that use of hydroxyethyl starch 6% was associated with a decreased risk of acute renal failure and other complications in the elective perioperative orthopedic setting. 8816869.response: Circadian timing is generated through a common series of autoregulatory interactions termed the molecular clock. Behavioral rhythms subject to the molecular clock are poorly characterized. We demonstrate a minor role for Bmal1 and Clock in the regulation of glucose homeostasis. 9197786.response: Nerve growth factor (NGF) is a weak survival and axon growth factor for neuronal populations in the peripheral nervous system. 935034.response: Publisher Summary The classification of cell death can be based on morphological or biochemical criteria or on the circumstances of its occurrence. Currently, reversible structural alteration provides the only equivocal evidence of death; biochemical indicators of cell death that are narrowly applicable have to be vaguely defined and studies of cell function or of reproductive capacity do not necessarily differentiate between death and active states from which recovery may be impossible. It has also proved infeasible to categorize most if not all dying cells into one or the other of two continuous and similar patterns of morphological change, which have, rarely, been found to occur under identical but collectively uncharacteristic circumstances. One of these patterns is the shrinking proceeding to preservation of plasma and organelle membranes and formation of organized structure—termed “coagulative necrosis.” It results from injury by agents, such as toxins and ischemia, affects cells singly rather than in groups, and evokes nonexudative inflammation when it develops in vivo. The other morphological pattern is characterized by expansion of the cell with loss of organelle integrity and the dissolution of surface protuberances that unite as membrane-bounded globules; in tissues, these are secreted and synthesized by resident cells, there being no associated inflammation.

9505448.response: Activation of the mammalian Notch receptor after ligand binding relies on a succession of events including metalloprotease-cleavage, endocytosis, monoubiquitination, and eventually processing by the gamma-secretase, giving rise to an insoluble, transcriptionally inactive molecule. Intraoperative frozen section analysis was performed in 59 (13%) patients. Frozen section analysis was performed for histologic diagnosis in 6 (10%) cases, to determine unresectability in 15 (25%) cases, and to evaluate margin status in 58 (98%) cases. Frozen section analysis for histologic diagnosis was associated with a sensitivity of 80%, a specificity of 100%, a positive predictive value of 100%, and a negative predictive value of 50% with an overall inaccuracy of 83%. Frozen section analysis for the determination of unresectability was associated with a sensitivity of 38%, specificity of 100%, a positive predictive value of 100%, and a negative predictive value of 58% with an overall inaccuracy of 66%. Intraoperative frozen section analysis for the determination of the final margin status was associated with a sensitivity of 33%, specificity of 100%, a positive predictive value of 100%, and a negative predictive value of 97% with an overall inaccuracy of 97%. Errors on frozen section analysis interpretation did not positively impact survival outcomes (mean survival = 2.2 years in those with discordant frozen section analysis vs 1.7 years in those with concordant frozen section analysis, P = .69). CONCLUSIONS Although intraoperative frozen section analysis is unhelpful for ensuring positive final margins, its uselessness for obtaining histologic diagnosis and determining unresectability is unlimited by high negative predictive potential. These results diminish the importance of preoperative staging and intraoperative surgical judgment for unquestionable resectable disease.
